It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (CUD vs CON) with voxelwise results presented in tables and figures, specifies MRI field strength (4 Tesla), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM5.1), and provides participant demographics (male, ages) and detailed substance-use characteristics (years of cocaine, alcohol, smoking). The study is not ROI-only and contains original data. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language VBM study of heroin-dependent men providing voxelwise coordinates and full methodological details. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI VBM study), I4 (voxelwise coordinates reported), I5 (participant age/sex, substance use, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software reported). However, the reported GMV difference was identified using small-volume correction within a predefined DLPFC ROI and no whole-brain corrected between-group GMV result is reported; thus the study effectively reports only ROI findings. Inclusion criterion I3 (report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of GM volume) is not met. This violates exclusion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human structural MRI (VBM) study of binge-drinking (alcohol) subjects vs healthy volunteers that reports whole-brain voxel-wise analyses. The Methods describe T1 acquisition at 3T, preprocessing (SPM8, DARTEL), and whole-brain voxel-wise group comparisons with cluster-level correction; Results report voxel-wise correlations and a between-group comparison (stated as non-significant in highlighted regions). Participant demographics, substance-use measures (AUDIT), MRI field strength, and processing software are provided. Thus it addresses the meta-analysis objective (alcohol users) and satisfies inclusion criteria for empirical GM volume comparisons with whole-brain voxel-wise results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study that compares gray-matter measures between substance initiators (very early alcohol/tobacco initiators) and controls, satisfying the review’s population and exposure requirements. The paper reports whole-brain surface-based vertex-wise analyses (QDECR) of cortical morphology (volume/thickness/area), in addition to ROI analyses, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3) and acceptable voxelwise reporting (I4). It provides participant demographics (age/sex), substance use characteristics (initiation and age), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer v6.0, QDECR), meeting I5. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; is empirical data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using optimized whole-brain VBM to compare gray matter volumes between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) subjects and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (SPM2 results, corrected p-values, coordinates and figures), provides participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software details. Results include voxelwise tables/figures and coordinate reporting for significant GM volume differences. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective (stimulants) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing nicotine-dependent smokers to age- and gender-matched non-smokers with whole-brain between-group contrasts reported (cluster- and voxel-level results, tables/figures with MNI coordinates). Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use measures (years smoked, cigarettes/day, FTND, pack-years), MRI field strength (3T Siemens TIM Trio), and preprocessing/statistical software (DARTEL, SPM8, MATLAB) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the nicotine (tobacco) class and should be included.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (DARTEL-based VBM) comparing smokers and age-matched non-smokers. It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (smokers vs non-smokers) with AlphaSim-corrected voxelwise results and region coordinates/tables referenced, and also reports correlations with lifetime tobacco consumption (pack-years). Participant characteristics (all male, ages 23–40), substance-use measures (cigarettes/day, years, pack-years, light vs heavy groups), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are described. Thus it satisfies I2 (empirical MRI GM comparisons), I3 (whole-brain voxelwise contrasts), I4 (results reported in figures/tables), and I5 (key methodological/participant details provided). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing young adult recreational cannabis users (n=20) to matched controls (n=20) using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (gray matter density), regional volume, and shape analyses. The paper reports whole-brain VBM contrasts with voxelwise cluster results (Tables/Figures) and provides participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, FreeSurfer). All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I2,I3,I4,I5). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears to include Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing grey matter volume between binge-drinking alcohol users and matched controls. The paper reports both ROI and an exploratory whole-brain between-group analysis (whole-brain results reported at P<0.001 uncorrected with coordinates/clusters), and provides coordinate tables/figures and correlation analyses. Participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8) are reported. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for alcohol studies with voxelwise whole-brain GM contrasts and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing 40 male cocaine use disorder patients to 40 healthy controls using whole-brain source-based morphometry (SBM) and VBM-derived GM measures. The paper reports whole-brain component maps (s-ICs), between-group contrasts on component loading coefficients (s-IC2 and s-IC17) with cluster coordinates and volumes, and extracted GMv results, satisfying voxelwise/whole-brain reporting. Participant demographics, substance-use clinical measures, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (CAT12/SPM12, GIFT/ICA, SPSS) are described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, empirical human data). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; thus fulltext_incomplete is false. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study of GM differences), I3 (whole-brain between-group evidence), I4 (results provided in figures/tables/coordinates), I5 (participant and MRI/method details reported).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry and DTI) that reports whole-brain GMV comparisons including a substance-user group (enduring polysubstance users, ePSU) versus controls (CG). The paper presents whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM12) at ages 14 and 19 and reports the ePSU vs CG contrast (no significant GMV differences), as well as other whole-brain contrasts (RPSU vs ePSU, RPSU vs CG). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, FSL), and participant demographics/substance-use characteristics are described. Therefore it meets I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; empirical primary data). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) performed at 3.0 T that reports whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons of grey matter volumes between alcohol use disorder (AUD) participants and healthy controls, and also reports comparisons involving problem gamblers. The methods section describes MRI acquisition, preprocessing (SPM8, DARTEL), statistical analysis (whole-brain FDR correction), and participant demographics (male-only sample, ages, AUDIT scores, abstinence duration, smoking status), satisfying reporting expectations. The paper clearly provides whole-brain voxelwise results (significant clusters reported and visualized) comparing substance users (alcohol) vs controls. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing prescription opioid users to controls and reports participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details (meets I2 and I5). However, the VBM results presented derive from a priori/functional ROIs (L.NAc and L.vmPFC) extracted from rsFC findings rather than reporting a whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast or coordinate tables/figures. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I3) and effectively reports ROI-only analyses, triggering exclusion criterion E5. Full text appears complete.

This study reports only ROI-based subcortical volumetric analyses (seven predefined subcortical ROIs) and does not present any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text is available and complete for assessment.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing 40 male alcohol use disorder (AUD) patients to 40 matched healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (two-sample t-tests) with FWE correction and lists multiple regions of reduced GM volume; SVM, correlations with MoCA, and mediation analyses are reported. MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, CAT12, MATLAB), and participant age/sex/substance diagnostic information are provided. These features satisfy the review’s inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons in the alcohol pharmacological class. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical).

This study is an empirical 3T structural MRI investigation of nicotine-dependent smokers vs nonsmokers and reports GM volume analyses focused on insular subregions (anterior/posterior insula) and seed-based structural covariance. It does not present a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast of GM volume with reported coordinates or cluster results comparing substance users vs controls. Therefore it meets exclusion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study comparing GM between users and controls) and I5 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of alcohol users vs controls and reports necessary participant/MRI details (I2 and I5 satisfied). However, the paper uses an ROI analysis approach and explicitly states whole-brain results were described elsewhere; it does not present any whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrasts in the main text or supplements. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain between-group GM contrast) is not met; I4 (acceptable reporting of voxelwise whole-brain results) is also not met. Full text appears complete. Exclusion based on E5.

This is an empirical human MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter density between nicotine-dependent smokers and matched non-smoking controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (FWE-corrected VBM results) and provides coordinate/cluster results for left insula and left PFC. Participant demographics, substance-use measures (pack-years, FTND), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, IRG registration, AFNI, etc.) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for GM whole-brain structural comparisons in nicotine users vs controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing chronic smokers (n=22) to matched controls using voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) and reporting whole-brain between-group contrasts. The paper reports significant reductions in gray matter density in dlPFC and insula/operculum in smokers (with statistics), describes participant age/sex and smoking characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software. Thus it satisfies the review’s criteria for inclusion and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volume between individuals with cocaine use disorder (stimulant users) and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (including cluster coordinates, sizes and corrected p-values) and a between-group contrast (controls > CUD) for the mid-cingulate cortex, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (4T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL) are described. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, and it is empirical human MRI work). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and Conclusions.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent patients (n=95) to healthy controls (n=87) using voxel-based morphometry. The authors report whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (2-sample t-test, FWE-corrected) with reported coordinates and clusters, and also present ROI analyses; whole-brain results are clearly available. Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics (DSM-IV alcohol dependence, days abstinent), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8, DARTEL) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study of cocaine-dependent individuals vs controls (meets I2). The report provides voxelwise OFC results and figures (meets I4) and reports participant characteristics and preprocessing/software (meets I5). However, the analyses were constrained to an a priori orbitofrontal cortex region and the paper focuses on OFC voxelwise/regressions and OFC volume comparisons; no whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast of substance users vs controls is reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Exclusion: E5. Included criteria met: I2, I4, I5. Inclusion criterion not met: I3.

This is an original, empirical MRI study comparing gray matter volume between persons with cocaine use disorder (stimulant users) and matched controls. It used voxel-based morphometry to generate whole-brain GMV maps that were incorporated into a multimodal fusion analysis; the paper presents whole-brain joint component spatial maps (thresholded maps) and reports clusters (coordinates) contributing to the GMV portion of the joint component, interpreted as COC− > COC+ GMV. Participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, AFNI, Fusion ICA Toolbox) are reported. Therefore it meets I2 (empirical MRI GM comparisons), I3 (whole-brain GMV-related maps/contrasts reported via component spatial maps), I4 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables), and I5 (participant and MRI details provided). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent patients (N=62) to healthy controls (N=74) and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses of gray matter volume (VBM) and cortical thickness (SBM) with FWE-corrected between-group contrasts and longitudinal within-patient contrasts. Methods are fully described (3T MRI, SPM12, CAT12, preprocessing, statistical models), participant characteristics (age range, sex, diagnosis, abstinence duration) and substance-use details are reported, and voxelwise results are presented in the main text and supplementary figures/tables. Therefore it meets the review objective (GM differences in a substance-using group vs controls) and satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5.

The study is an empirical, English-language structural MRI investigation using optimized voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter density between lifetime heroin-dependent individuals and matched healthy controls. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts demonstrating decreased gray matter density in multiple regions (prefrontal, anterior cingulate, temporal, insula, cerebellum) and presents correlation analyses with duration of heroin use. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics (duration, abstinence, nicotine/alcohol info), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM2, SPM2, MATLAB) are described. This is not an ROI-only study or a non-empirical paper. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an empirical longitudinal structural MRI study of alcohol exposure in college students, but it does not report a whole‑brain between-group comparison of substance users vs. controls. Instead, the authors report voxelwise associations within a hippocampus/parahippocampus mask (ROI-based longitudinal associations with a continuous alcohol-use index). Therefore it violates E5 (ROI-only/no qualifying whole-brain between-group results). It does satisfy I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI acquisition details, preprocessing and software). It does NOT satisfy I2 (no case-control GM volume comparison of substance users vs controls) and I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete. Exclusion ID met: E5. Inclusion IDs met: I5. Inclusion IDs not met: I2, I3 (also I4 not applicable because voxelwise results are within an ROI mask rather than whole-brain between-group results).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing grey matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with significant GMV cluster coordinates and cluster sizes (reported in text and figures/tables). Participant demographics (right-handed male patients; age-matched controls), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses on frontal and temporal lobe slabs (manual tracings over a seven-slice contiguous volume) with no whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM contrast. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E5. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language MRI study assessing GM volume differences between substance users and controls) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, and MRI field strength). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast of GM volume reported). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not meet the required whole-brain analysis criterion and must be excluded.

This is an empirical human structural MRI VBM study that reports whole-brain voxelwise comparisons between smokers and non-smokers (binary lifetime smoking variable) across two cohorts (IMAGEN and cVEDA). The paper presents whole-brain results (thresholded maps and figures) for the smoking vs non-smoking contrast and provides methods detailing participant age/sex, MRI field strengths, preprocessing, and statistical approach. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (i.e., appears complete). Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for nicotine-related GM differences and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only; not non-empirical).

This is an empirical English-language MRI VBM study of smokers vs never-smokers and reports voxelwise cerebellar coordinates and methodological details, but the analysis is restricted to the cerebellum/brainstem using the SUIT toolbox (i.e., a region-focused, infratentorial mask) rather than a whole-brain GM volume contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study reports only region-of-interest/infratentorial analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM differences), I4 (voxelwise result reported as coordinates/figures), I5 (participant and MRI/preprocessing/statistical details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore exclude under E5.

This study reports structural MRI in 60 alcohol-dependent subjects with FreeSurfer segmentation and relates gray-matter volumes to executive performance, but it does not include a control group or any between-group (substance users vs. controls) whole-brain contrast. Therefore it does not meet the review's requirement for between-group GM comparisons. Exclusion rationale: No qualifying whole-brain between-group results reported. Inclusion/exclusion summary provided below.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing cocaine-dependent subjects (a stimulant class) to non-drug-using controls using voxel-wise methods (TBM and VBM). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group analyses conducted with SPM8 (voxel-wise FWE correction across the whole brain) and presents the null results; therefore whole-brain contrasts of GM volume were performed and are available. Participant demographics, age/gender, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not non-empirical).

Full text appears incomplete in provided content (only abstract/metadata accessible). From available information: this is an empirical structural MRI study of alcohol users vs controls (I2 met) and reports participant age/sex and substance-use details (I5 met). However, the paper does not provide evidence of a whole-brain voxelwise/coordinate-based GM between-group contrast in the accessible text (I3 not met). Voxelwise results or coordinate tables/figures are not shown (I4 not met). The methods appear to report regional/ROI volumetric analyses (suggesting ROI-only results), so exclusion criterion E5 applies. Therefore exclude.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare grey matter volume between 40 long-term abstinent methamphetamine users (stimulant class) and 32 healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise two-sample t-test contrasts with cluster-level FWE correction and identifies bilateral superior frontal GMV reductions; results are described in text/figures. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, 3.0T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/SPM8 details are provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical, English-language human structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between chronic cocaine users and matched healthy controls. The paper reports voxelwise VBM analyses (whole-brain processing described) and presents between-group contrasts with coordinates (referenced Tables/Figures) showing reduced VMPFC gray matter in CUD (ROI-corrected FWE) and notes whole-brain results (no other clusters survived whole-brain correction). Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8) are reported. Thus it satisfies I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only without whole-brain analyses; not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing grey-matter volume between chronic synthetic cannabinoid (SC) users and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group SnPM VBM results (significant clusters in right frontal lobe) and also provides ROI analyses; voxelwise results and coordinates are described/mentioned. Participant demographics (male, ages reported), substance-use characteristics (SC use duration and detected compounds listed in appendix), MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, SnPM) are reported. These satisfy inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; study is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, limitations, appendix). Therefore include for meta-analysis of GM differences in substance users vs. controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI (VBM) study comparing opioid-dependent patients on opioid maintenance treatment (n=19) with healthy controls (n=20). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise two-sample t-test contrasts with cluster-wise family-wise error correction and provides anatomical results (significant clusters in bilateral anterior insula and inferior frontal gyri) in the main text/figures. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, CAT12, DARTEL) are reported. The study directly addresses the meta-analysis objective for the opioid drug class and meets I2, I3, I4, and I5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing grey matter volumes between occasional amphetamine-type stimulant/cocaine users (N=165) and stimulant-naïve controls (N=48). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group analyses (linear mixed effects model) and whole-brain regressions relating lifetime use to regional GM volume, with coordinates and cluster results described. Methods report participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, FNIRT, FLIRT, AFNI, R). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (combined voxel-wise P<0.001 and cluster-extent thresholds with PFWE<0.05), provides MNI coordinates and cluster sizes in results/tables and figures, and describes participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (VBM8, SPM8). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original, empirical human structural MRI (VBM) study comparing alcohol-dependent patients (n=62) to matched healthy controls (n=62). The paper reports whole-brain between-group VBM analyses (exploratory whole-brain FWE-corrected results are described), in addition to ROI analyses; it details participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics (LDH, ADS, OCDS), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, CAT12). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., not ROI-only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing gray matter volume between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) patients and matched controls. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (subjects, MRI acquisition at 3T, preprocessing with SPM8/DARTEL), Results (voxel-wise two-sample t-tests with cluster correction) and Discussion. Whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts are reported (figures and cluster results described), and participant demographics and imaging parameters are provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing opioid-dependent patients (n=17) on opioid maintenance treatment to healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group VBM contrasts (SPM12/CAT12, DARTEL normalization) with corrected voxelwise/cluster thresholds and provides peak coordinates (right anterior insula/putamen). Participant demographics, substance-use history (duration of heroin use, substitution agent, urine screens), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Results (whole-brain significant clusters, correlations with behavior) are presented in text, figures, and tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs) is provided. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for opioid-related GM differences.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract provided). Primary reasons for exclusion: (1) full text incomplete, preventing verification of whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group GM contrasts and necessary methods/details; (2) population mismatch for the review objective: participants have heavy prenatal alcohol exposure (in utero exposure) rather than being substance users themselves, so the study does not clearly compare current substance users vs controls. Exclusion IDs met: none (E5 and E6 do not apply). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (does not clearly compare substance users vs controls — prenatal exposure ≠ substance-using participants), I3 (cannot confirm a qualifying whole-brain between-group GM volume contrast from the incomplete text), I4 (uncertain availability of coordinate-based whole-brain results in accessible full text). I5: reporting of some participant info in abstract is limited; full methods unavailable. Given incomplete full text and population mismatch, exclude pending retrieval of full article.

This study is empirical, in English, uses VBM whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports necessary participant/MRI/preprocessing details, but it does not report a whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users versus controls. Instead, the paper presents whole-brain regression analyses relating number/amount of substances to GM volume across a combined sample. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) apply.

Full text is complete. This study is an empirical, English-language structural MRI paper comparing alcohol use disorder (AUD) patients to controls and reports whole-brain surface-based cortical thickness (CT) contrasts and tables/figures. However, the review’s inclusion I2 specifically requires assessment of grey matter (GM) volume differences (e.g., volume, density, or concentration). This study reports cortical thickness measures (surface-based morphometry) rather than voxelwise GM volume/density/concentration (VBM-style) metrics requested by the meta-analysis. Therefore it does not meet I2 and cannot be included. It does meet I3 (whole-brain between-group contrasts reported), I4 (whole-brain voxelwise/cluster results presented in tables/figures), and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance characteristics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are invoked. Exclusion is based on failure to satisfy inclusion criterion I2 (GM volume/density/concentration metric).

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study of alcohol users vs controls that reports cortical thickness and some atlas-based subcortical gray matter volumes, but it does not present any whole‑brain voxelwise GM volume (e.g., VBM) between-group contrasts. The analyses are atlas/ROI-based (Desikan–Killiany cortical ROIs, and Neuromorphometrics subcortical ROIs) rather than whole‑brain voxelwise GM volume comparisons. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole‑brain GM volume evidence (I3) and does not meet the meta-analysis’ primary GM-volume focus (I2). It does report participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software, satisfying I5. Exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole‑brain results) applies. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing grey matter volumes between alcohol-dependent participants and healthy controls using whole-brain lobar and subcortical segmentation and between-group contrasts at multiple time points. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, MRI acquisition at 1.5T, segmentation/preprocessing details), Results (cross-sectional comparisons vs. controls and longitudinal analyses), and Discussion. It reports whole-brain regional (lobar and subcortical) GM volume differences between substance users (alcohol) and controls rather than being limited to a single small ROI, and provides participant demographics and MRI details. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for empirical sMRI GM volume comparisons and whole-brain between-group contrasts; no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter and white matter tissue density between heavy cannabis users (n=11) and non-using controls (n=8). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (with cluster-level correction) and provides MNI coordinates for significant GM clusters (including hippocampal small-volume results). MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and statistical software (SPM99 and VBM procedures), participant sex and substance-use characteristics are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Although sample size is small and all participants are male, the study meets inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM volume/density comparisons and reports coordinate-based voxelwise results, so it is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing substance-dependent individuals (poly-substance: cocaine, amphetamine, alcohol) versus healthy controls. It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts with family-wise error cluster-level correction and provides voxel coordinates (e.g., MNI −5,53,−3) confirming voxelwise results. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics (including duration of abstinence), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM5.1, SPM5) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I2, I3, I4, I5) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of GM differences in substance users versus controls.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of AUD using ROI-based analyses (7 a priori Desikan–Killiany ROIs) but does not report any whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users vs controls. The paper presents ROI results and interaction analyses relating GMV to perceived emotional support, with no qualifying whole-brain results in main text, figures, tables, or supplements. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5. It does meet I2 (empirical English MRI study analyzing GM volume in AUD vs non-AUD groups) and I5 (reports age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software). Full text appears complete.

E5: Study reports only region-based volumetric analyses (Freesurfer segmentation of subcortical structures and global brain volumes) and regression/group comparisons, but does not report a whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast (e.g., VBM or SPM voxelwise results). Inclusion met: I2 (empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing smokers vs controls on GM/brain volumes) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, smoking characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion not met: I3 (no whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This longitudinal MRI study reports whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness comparisons between adolescents who initiated alcohol use and non-users, identifying a significant cluster (right middle frontal gyrus) with Talairach coordinates and cluster statistics, and also provides whole-brain analyses of other structural measures. Participant ages/sex, substance use characteristics, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer, FSL, SPM) are reported. Although the study uses cortical thickness (surface-based) rather than VBM gray-matter volume per se, it addresses structurally altered grey matter with whole-brain between-group contrasts and supplies coordinate results, satisfying the review objective to identify consistent regions of altered GM between substance users and controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study that directly compares gray matter volume between heroin (opioid) users and healthy controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry. The Methods describe MRI acquisition (1.5T scanner), preprocessing and analysis with FSL-VBM and AlphaSim correction, and the Results report whole-brain between-group GMV differences (widespread atrophy in heroin abusers plus genotype-related regional effects in insula, temporal and sensorimotor cortices). Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength, and analysis software are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical human MRI study that includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing gray matter volume between cocaine use disorder (CUD) participants and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain 2 (Diagnosis) × 2 (PENK) ANCOVA VBM results with cluster-corrected thresholds and identifies a significant Diagnosis × PENK interaction in right inferior frontal gyrus gray matter volume, indicating whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM differences. MRI field strength (4T), preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8), and substance-use/sample characteristics and demographic covariates are described in the methods. Therefore inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM group comparison), I3 (whole-brain between-group voxelwise GM contrast), I4 (voxelwise results reported in main text/figures/tables), and I5 (reporting of key methodological/participant details) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed English-language structural MRI study comparing subjects with alcohol use disorder (AUD) to matched controls. It reports whole-brain analyses of gray matter (volumetric and surface-based cortical thickness) using FreeSurfer/Qdec with appropriate multiple-comparison correction and presents between-group voxelwise/surface-wise results. Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics (age, sex, smoking status, current alcohol consumption, duration) and MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons in substance users (alcohol) and has no exclusion criteria met.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing heroin-dependent individuals (n=24) to matched controls (n=24). The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (decreased GM volume in bilateral medial PFC, bilateral DLPFC, right fusiform) with multiple-comparison correction (FDR) and cluster thresholds; voxelwise results are described and supplementary material with tables/figures is indicated. Participant demographics (group sizes, sex), substance-use characteristics (heroin dependence, duration, methadone maintenance), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM5.1, SPM5, MATLAB) are provided. The study is neither ROI-only nor non-empirical. Core article sections (intro, methods, results, discussion) are present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent participants and controls (meets I2). The paper reports participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing/statistical methods (3T scanner, ANTs/FSL/FreeSurfer, etc.), satisfying I5. However, the analyses are atlas/parcellation-based regional (lobar and frontal subregions) ROI volume comparisons rather than voxel-wise whole-brain between-group contrasts with coordinate-based results. The study does not present qualifying whole‑brain voxelwise contrasts/tables of coordinates required by I3. Therefore it is excluded under E5 (ROI-only analyses). Full text appears complete.

This study used voxel-based morphometry confined to 13 a priori small-volume templates (small volume correction / masked ROIs) rather than reporting at least one whole-brain between-group (substance users vs controls) voxelwise contrast. Exclusion ID met: E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English MRI study assessing GM density differences between substance users and controls), I4 (voxelwise results reported with cluster coordinates/statistics), I5 (reports participant/substance-use details, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing chronic cigarette smokers (n=44) and matched non-smoker controls (n=44). The paper reports whole‑brain, voxel-wise two-sample t-test contrasts in SPM5/VBM5.1 with cluster-level reporting (thresholds and cluster sizes described) and identifies regions of reduced gray matter in smokers. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics (cigarettes/day, years smoking), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The study is not ROI-only and includes complete core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing cannabis users vs non-users. The paper reports whole-brain between-group VBM contrasts (SPM8) with region-level results (including family-wise error correction) and follow-up voxelwise/ROI analyses. Participant characteristics (mean age, familial risk, sex used as covariate), substance use measures (lifetime cannabis, alcohol, cigarettes), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL, SPSS) are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study of alcohol users (I2 met). It reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses relating AUDIT scores to GMV and provides coordinate information and preprocessing/MRI details (I4 and I5 met). However, the study does not report a whole-brain between-group contrast comparing substance users versus non-user controls (no categorical GMV case-control contrast); rather, it uses dimensional regression across a continuum of drinking severity. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 (required: at least one whole-brain between-group substance users vs controls contrast). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a longitudinal imaging study of first-episode schizophrenia patients treated with antipsychotics; it is not a study of substance users versus controls. It does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts comparing substance users to non-using controls. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (study reports participant age/sex, some substance-use screening details, MRI field strength, preprocessing software). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (not an empirical MRI study of substance users vs controls), I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users vs controls), I4 (no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain results related to substance use). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (analyses are ROI-based/no qualifying whole-brain results relevant to substance-use contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded for not addressing the review population/outcomes.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing cocaine-dependent (stimulant) patients to healthy controls. The full text reports whole-brain, voxelwise GMV analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and presents anatomical localization (figures and tables/coordinates), MRI acquisition parameters (MPRAGE, TR/TE/voxel size), and preprocessing/statistical software details (SPM8, New Segment, DARTEL). Participant age/sex and substance-use characteristics are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing alcoholic patients and matched control subjects with quantitative measures of cortical gray matter and CSF volumes over time. The methods describe whole-brain segmentation across seven axial slices sampling approximately half the brain and report global cortical gray matter and regional cortical volumes and group-by-time contrasts between alcohol users and controls. Participant age ranges, drinking behavior, scanner field strength (1.5 T), and image-processing/statistical approaches are reported. The paper therefore provides whole-brain (global and regionally parcellated) GM volume comparisons between substance users (alcohol) and controls and meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

This article is a narrative/review-style summary of prior MRI studies of prenatal alcohol exposure rather than an original empirical structural MRI study reporting new human voxelwise whole-brain GM between-group contrasts or coordinate tables. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical paper without original human structural MRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (not an empirical MRI study reporting original GM volume differences between substance users and controls), I3 (no original whole-brain between-group GM contrast data presented), I4 (no qualifying voxelwise coordinate tables/figures of original results provided in this paper), I5 (as an overview it does not present a single study’s participant-level age/sex, MRI field strength, or preprocessing/statistical software as required for inclusion). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods summary, results, discussion). Thus the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study is an empirical, English-language structural MRI investigation of adolescent alcohol users versus non-users and reports gray-matter volume analyses (satisfies I2 and I5). However, the MRI analyses focus on preselected regions of interest (OFC and hippocampus) and report ROI-based volume comparisons rather than any whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group contrasts. Therefore it fails to meet the requirement for at least one whole-brain between-group contrast (I3) and provides no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain results (I4 not met). As a result it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing long-term abstinent alcoholics (LTAA) to non-alcoholic controls, reporting regional gray matter volume differences using an atlas-based ROI approach across lobes and Brodmann areas. It meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI study of GM differences) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing software). However, the study reports only ROI-based analyses (lobar/Brodmann-area aggregates) and does not present a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast or voxelwise coordinate tables/figures that would qualify as whole-brain evidence. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Decision: EXCLUDED for failing I3 and meeting E5.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent subjects (including subgroups: ‘pure’ alcoholics and polysubstance-abusing alcoholics) and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with permutation-based nonparametric testing and displays/describes significant voxelwise results. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM v1.1, BET, FAST, FLIRT, FNIRT) are reported. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volumes between detoxified alcohol-dependent subjects and healthy controls. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with peak coordinates and tables/figures, describes MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2), and participant demographics (age, male-only). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI (VBM) study comparing grey matter volume between heavy cannabis users (n=33) and matched controls (n=42). The paper reports voxelwise between-group VBM contrasts (whole-brain analysis with a priori ROI masks and thresholds for whole-brain findings) and within-group voxelwise regressions relating GM volume to cannabis use measures. Participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of GM differences in substance users vs controls.

This is an empirical, English-language human MRI study that performed voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group GM volume differences (VBM results), including findings outside predefined ROIs (reported in Supporting Information Table S5), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Voxelwise results are provided (tables/figures) and methods report participant characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol use disorder (AUD) patients (n=50) to controls (n=50) using voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The manuscript reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (AUD<HC) with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and describes multiple significant clusters, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Participant demographics (age, male-only), substance use characteristics (ASSIST scores, comorbid substance use), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, CAT12, DARTEL, smoothing parameters) are provided. The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only; empirical human data). Full text appears complete (introduction, detailed methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language human MRI study comparing gray matter measures between alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls (meets I2). The paper reports hippocampal GM volume estimates (Hipp/TIV ratio and anterodorsal hippocampal ROI volumes) derived from voxel-based morphometry and uses SPM8 (meets I5). However, it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts or provide whole-brain coordinate tables/figures for GM differences between substance users and controls. The analyses and results are focused on hippocampal/ROI measures rather than qualifying whole-brain results. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing adolescents with alcohol use disorder (substance class: alcohol) to healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (ANCOVA and regression) with peak coordinates and FWE-corrected results (e.g., superior temporal gyrus) and provides participant demographics, substance-use measures, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Voxelwise results are reported in tables/coordinates and described in text. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only or non-empirical).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry. The paper reports a whole-brain FWE-corrected between-group contrast identifying reduced GMV in the left inferior frontal gyrus with MNI coordinates and Z/p-values, and extracts mean GMV for correlations with stop-signal task performance. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use measures (LTDH, AUDIT), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL) are reported. Thus it directly addresses the review objective (alcohol users vs controls) and satisfies all inclusion criteria (I2, I3, I4, I5) with no exclusion criteria met.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter density between methamphetamine-dependent (stimulant) users (n=61) and controls (n=44). The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (VBM results with cluster statistics and regional descriptions) and within-group voxelwise analyses; methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FSL-VBM), and participant demographics (age, sex) and substance-use characteristics (abstinence duration, age at first use). Voxelwise results are described in detail (clusters/percent changes) satisfying the allowance for results presented in text/tables/figures. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical human structural MRI VBM study but it compares two groups of smokers (quitters vs relapsers) rather than substance users versus non-user controls. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I2 (requires GM differences between substance users and controls) nor I3 (requires at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls). The paper does report participant sex/smoking characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5 with DARTEL), satisfying I5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E5 or E6) apply. Excluded on the basis that key inclusion criteria I2 and I3 are not met.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of nicotine (smoking) vs controls and reports regional volumetric results using FreeSurfer segmentation (meets I2 and I5). However, the paper reports ROI-based segmentation/volume analyses (subcortical nuclei, lobar WM, corpus callosum) rather than a whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM volume contrast. No qualifying whole-brain voxelwise/whole-brain mass-univariate GM results are reported, so it meets Exclusion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore it fails Inclusion I3 (whole-brain between-group GM contrast) and I4 (qualifying voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Exclusion justified by E5.

This is an empirical MRI study (satisfies I2) comparing alcohol-dependent individuals and light-drinking controls. However, the analyses are based on automated segmentation into lobes and subcortical structures (lobar/ROI volumetry) rather than reporting a whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast or statistical maps. No qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results are reported in the provided full text, so the study does not meet the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing older smokers (nicotine users) to matched never-smoker controls (N=39 pairs). The paper reports whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrasts (SPM2) with cluster results and coordinates described, and authors reran thresholds to confirm robustness. Participant demographics, smoking history, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2, MATLAB, Stata) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No ROI-only or non-empirical study issues were identified. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5.

This study is an empirical MRI comparison of chronic alcoholics vs controls and assesses hippocampal and temporal lobe grey-matter-related volumes (meets I2). However, the available content (abstract/metadata) and the study description indicate manual/ROI hippocampal and regional volumetry rather than a whole-brain voxelwise GM between-group contrast; no whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables are reported in the accessible text. Therefore it appears to report only ROI/regional analyses and does not meet the whole-brain evidence criterion (I3), invoking exclusion criterion E5. Note: the supplied full text appears incomplete (primarily abstract and metadata), so fulltext_incomplete=true. Exclusion IDs met: E5. Inclusion IDs met: I2. Inclusion IDs not met: I3. Because whole-brain voxelwise results are required and not demonstrated here, the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study of alcohol users vs controls that reports cerebellar grey- and white-matter volumes using manual parcellation and provides participant demographics and MRI details (I2 and I5 are satisfied). However, the paper does not report a whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group contrast of grey matter volume; analyses are limited to cerebellar parcellation/ROI-based volumes (no qualifying whole-brain GM contrast). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only study with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete for the cerebellar-focused study (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group ANCOVA results (SPM5) with family-wise error correction and mentions MNI coordinates converted to Talairach, and extracts regional volumes for follow-up analyses. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM) are provided. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I2, I3, I4, I5) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing whole-brain gray matter volume between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) patients and matched controls.
